multiplechoiceresponse.p: A colleague asks a public AI chat to summarize a document containing customer addresses and account numbers. What is the core problem?

choice.div: Restricted data has left the organization's systems.
The document was too long for the tool.

div.p: Accuracy is secondary here: the paste itself is the transfer. Restricted data stays in the system that owns it.

multiplechoiceresponse.p: You delete the conversation after pasting. What have you actually controlled?

choice.div: Your copy in the interface — not the transfer or any provider retention.
The provider's copy, which is removed with the chat.
Nothing at all, so deleting is pointless.

div.p: Deletion is a tidy-up, not a data-retention control. The decision has to be made before the paste.

multiplechoiceresponse.p: Which is the safest way to draft a reply about a specific customer complaint?

choice.div: Replace identifying detail with placeholders, draft, then fill in details inside the owning system.
Paste the complaint with the name removed but the account number kept.
Paste it into a personal account so it is not linked to work.

div.p: Placeholders remove the data while keeping the shape of the task. A personal account makes the exposure worse, not better.

choiceresponse.p: Which items are restricted and must not be pasted into a chat tool? Select all that apply.

div.p: Personal, financial, health, safeguarding and credential data are restricted. A published report is public.
